summary: Remote-controlled shell agent: WebSocket-driven PTY on installer host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent runs as a persistent background service (installed via systemd/launchd/PM2) that opens an outbound WebSocket to a configured server URL and pipes inbound messages into a locally-spawned PTY (bash on Linux/macOS, PowerShell on Windows). Any party that controls the configured server endpoint and holds the shared agentSecret can execute arbitrary shell commands on the installer's host, read and write arbitrary files, drive git operations, and trigger a self-upgrade path that runs `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` and respawns the service. The agent also modifies shell PATH via service/linux.js to include ~/.local/bin and ~/.npm-global/bin at install/service-setup time. While the package's advertised purpose is remote agent control, the shipped configuration establishes a network-to-shell dataflow on the installer's machine: a remote operator holding the secret has full interactive shell access equivalent to a reverse shell.
